name: uw_hub_partner_age
label_authority: Elicit run of 25 Oct 2026 as saved. The per-paper distinctions are the tool's claim; no human verification. DOIs for three targets come from other reference exports in notes/test-questions/.
identity_rule: DOI or verified work identity; title-only matches require adjudication
question: Has any published work scheduled entanglement distribution at a quantum switch or hub that serves two bipartite requests sharing one user (for example A-B and A-C), where the hub chooses the swap partner from the age of the stored link, minimizes the age of entanglement under a memory cutoff, and adds a long-run delivery-rate floor and an attempt budget? Has this been studied for underwater optical quantum links?
reference: Elicit research agent, Balanced, 25 Oct 2026, saved in notes/test-questions/uw-hub-partner-by-link-age/. The same question was asked in DEIXIS by the owner the same evening. DOIs were not shown in the answer; three were resolved from other saved exports, four have none.
expected_direction: No exact match located and no underwater version; the possible contribution is the combination, not any single part. The distinction the answer must draw: stored-link age (the physical age of an elementary link) versus time since the request was last served (AoEE). Mitrolaris 2026 allows overlapping user subsets but discards unused links each slot and constrains per-slot memory capacity, not a long-run delivery floor plus attempt budget. Inesta 2023 keeps stored-link ages and cutoffs in an MDP but minimises end-to-end delivery time on a repeater chain. Underwater work covers the channel only.

answer_elements.question: Closest quantum-switch precedents, and which part of the question each one covers
Stored-link age versus time since the request was last served, as an explicit distinction
Stored-link ages with cutoffs inside an MDP, and why a repeater chain differs from a shared-user hub
Underwater optical links: channel feasibility only, with no hub scheduler located
No exact match stated as a search result rather than proof, with the contribution placed in the conjunction of the three parts

pass_rule.status: draft from QUESTION.md, not confirmed by the owner
rules: The answer separates three things: AoE scheduling at a switch (known), partner choice by stored-link age with a shared user (the study's angle), and the underwater setting.
It names the closest switch and AoE scheduling papers with located passages and says which part of the question each one covers.
It does not claim novelty from finding nothing; "no match found" is stated as a search result, not as proof.
DEIXIS passes if it finds at least Mitrolaris 2026 and Inesta 2023 from located passages and draws the same age distinction.
